reading: The output is a fixed 3x3 pattern of 8s chosen by the dominant non-background colour of the input: 1 -> 008/880/080, 2 -> 000/888/000, 3 -> 088/080/080.

slots.feature: the most frequent non-zero colour of the input
slots.lookup: learned table colour -> fixed 3x3 pattern of 8 on 0 (1:008/880/080, 2:000/888/000, 3:088/080/080)

why: on every pair the output equals the table entry for the input's most common non-zero colour

reading: Each isolated coloured cell gets a 3x3 ring around it, ring colour set by the cell's colour (3 -> 6, 8 -> 4, 2 -> 1); the centre stays.
why: every marker is the centre of a 3x3 square ring whose colour is a fixed function of the marker colour; all other cells unchanged

reading: The 3x3 input is tiled into a square of (number of background cells) x (number of background cells) blocks; the first k blocks in row-major order hold a copy, where k is the number of coloured cells, the rest are empty.
why: output side = 3 * (#bg cells); blocks 1..#fg (row-major) equal the input, all other blocks are 0
invariants: each filled block is an exact copy of the input

reading: Every input cell is enlarged to a 3x3 block of its colour (scale up by 3).
why: output cell (y,x) equals input cell (y//3, x//3)

reading: Four single marker cells (colour 5) bound a rectangle; draw its outline one cell inside the markers, in the colour of the other shape, keeping everything else.

slots.bounds: top = top marker row + 1, bottom = bottom marker row - 1, left = left marker col + 1, right = right marker col - 1

why: the added cells are exactly the outline of the rectangle inset by one from the four markers, coloured like the shape

reading: The grid is cut into equal cells by separator lines; one cell holds a pattern, which is copied into every cell whose row and column indices have the same parity as the source cell (every second cell in both directions).

slots.unit: contents of the one non-empty compartment
slots.anchors: compartments whose compartment-row and compartment-column index differ from the source's by even numbers

why: every compartment with the source's parity in both directions equals the source; others stay empty

reading: The top row is a colour key k0,k1,k2,...; the single cell of colour k0 below the separator becomes the centre of concentric square rings, ring at distance d coloured k_d.

slots.centre: the single marker cell below the separator
slots.key: the colour sequence in the top row left to right
slots.ring colour: ring at Chebyshev distance d gets key[d]
slots.extent: as many rings as key entries (0 entries draw background), clipped by the grid

why: every cell at Chebyshev distance d from the marker has colour key[d] for d < key length

reading: A 2x2 block [a b / c d] gets four 2x2 blocks added diagonally off its corners, each coloured with the diagonally opposite cell: d at top-left, c at top-right, b at bottom-left, a at bottom-right (clipped at the border).

slots.subject: the 2x2 multicoloured block
slots.anchors: the four 2x2 positions diagonally adjacent to its corners
slots.colour: the colour of the block cell diagonally opposite that corner

why: each corner 2x2 region is filled with the opposite corner's colour; the original block is unchanged

reading: Four L-shaped corner brackets mark each box; the 1-pattern inside each box is completed to be symmetric about the box centre (mirror left-right or top-bottom, whichever half is empty), and stray 1s outside all boxes are erased.

slots.part: each box bounded by four corner brackets
slots.subject: the 1-cells inside the box
slots.axis: the box's vertical or horizontal centre line (the one across which the pattern is one-sided)

why: inside every box the 1-pattern is symmetric about the box centre line; no 1 lies outside a box

reading: Full separator lines cut the grid into compartments; the top-left compartment is filled with 1, the centre compartment with 2, and the bottom-right compartment with 3.

slots.targets: top-left compartment, middle compartment (middle row-band x middle column-band), bottom-right compartment

why: exactly those three compartments are filled with 1, 2, 3; everything else unchanged
